result.title: Variational Cognitive Memory Abstraction for Long-Horizon Vision-Language-Action Models
result.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown remarkable success in robotic manipulation, yet their ability to execute long-horizon tasks remains limited by insufficient long- term memory modeling. Existing methods either rely on implicit temporal representations within policy networks, where historical information can be gradually diluted, or maintain explicit memory buffers that suffer from redundancy, noise accumulation, and inefficient retrieval. In this paper, we propose CogMemory, a novel variational cognitive memory framework that enables VLA systems to selectively preserve and reuse task-relevant historical information. Our approach encodes multimodal trajectories into compact latent memory representations through a selective state- space memory encoder, multi-slot temporal abstraction, and variational information compression. During action generation, dynamic cross-attention retrieval with gated fusion adaptively incorporates relevant memories into policy prediction. With merely 3.45M additional parameters, CogMemory stays lightweight and seamlessly fits both early- and intermediate-fusion VLA backbones. Extensive experiments on long-horizon robotic manipulation benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements across diverse VLA backbones.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 CogMemory，用选择性状态空间编码器、多槽时间抽象与变分压缩把多模态轨迹写成紧凑 latent 记忆，动作生成时通过动态 cross-attention 检索与门控融合注入策略；仅增 3.45M 参数，可接入早期/中期融合 VLA backbone。
AI.relevance_reason: 其 latent 记忆的变分压缩与门控检索可供核查 LVR 中视觉信息保留、压缩坍缩与记忆贡献分配问题，但任务是机器人长程操作，未涉及推理轨迹或停止决策，联系属方法借鉴。
